I agree with those points.

Companies will largely be following the money. Hence DLC, buggy releases, early access. We can and should make it known when a company behaves in a bad manner. Whether it is a poor technical performance or a poor story or censorship, we should point it out.

People can say that they boycott a given practice and can argue in favour of other people doing so. The canonical example in gaming is preorders. Some of us are adamant that people should not be preordering. I'm very happy not doing that. There are many old games I haven't played yet so I don't feel the need to pay for something I can't even play yet.

Unfortunately it seems like some of the censorship happens after release. Was it Broken Chalice which had a problematic gravestone removed after release? When you've already paid there's not much you can do when Steam will gladly remove things for you (that's another story). A boycott doesn't help much there when they already have your money. Similarly when a localisation never happens you can't really boycott something you can't buy.

I don't really know why people advocated against organised boycotts in the beginning. I assume it has something to do with people wanting to support devs and not wanting to behave like the SJWs. We want to build things up rather than tear things down. We want to encourage devs to develop games as they want. If they are convinced that they should change some concept because they feel it is bad then they should be free to make that change. Are we going to say that their choice was wrong, basically mirroring the SJW argument?
